issues.source_quote: Тебя терзают смутные сомнения / Меня терзают смутные сомнения
issues.translation_quote: I'm tormented by vague doubts
issues.justification: The famous quoted line (Ilf & Petrov, 'Twelve Chairs') is rendered flatly; the parodic, quotational high register is lost.

issues.translation_quote: when will this end?
issues.justification: The pun on 'кончится' (end/finish, with an innuendo in the reply 'Сейчас заканчиваю') is lost; the reply 'I'm just finishing' doesn't carry the double entendre.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Spare my life, Great Sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: Stock formula 'не вели казнить, вели слово молвить' is mangled; 'our hope' is an awkward calque of 'надежа', and the later 'Let me speak a word' is disconnected.

issues.source_quote: Отведай ты из моего кубка! ... Здрав будь, боярин! ... Ключница водку делала?
issues.translation_quote: Taste thou from my goblet! ... Be thou in health, boyar! ... Thou hast made such a machine?
issues.justification: Pseudo-archaic 'thou/thee/hath' is inconsistent (mixed with modern speech in the same lines) and reads as Shakespearean pastiche, not Muscovite Russian; the comic contrast between Ivan's speech and modern speech is blurred and uneven.

issues.translation_quote: Go-al! Go-al!
issues.justification: The chant 'Шайбу, шайбу' (hockey fans' 'puck!') is mistranslated as a soccer 'goal' chant, losing the specific reference and anachronism joke.

issues.translation_quote: Keep your mouth open!
issues.justification: The dentist context is rendered without the sense of a receptionist's call; the line is a mistranslation of the Russian 'Don't close your mouth' to the patient, fine, but 'Keep your mouth open' loses the jokey rebuke to the busy dentist's patient.

issues.source_quote: Вы с магнитофоном пришли к Шпаку?
issues.translation_quote: And did you come to Shpak's with a tape recorder?
issues.justification: Fine literally, but the source is a running suspicion gag; more importantly 'Тьфу на Вас' rendered as 'Pah on you' is unnatural and loses the colloquial spit-curse.

issues.translation_quote: The Tambov wolf is your boyar!
issues.justification: The idiom 'Тамбовский волк тебе товарищ' (Tambov wolf is your comrade) is a fixed Soviet insult; rendering is literal and the joke does not land for English viewers.

issues.translation_quote: Profession de foi!
issues.justification: The wordplay is a mock-French jab at 'профессиональная обязанность' (professional duty) and 'profession de foi' means a statement of beliefs; the pun relies on sound ('профессия'), unexplained in English.

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих.
issues.translation_quote: Der grosser König, das schwedischen Königsreich, sandte mich. Seinen treuen Diener, zu Ihnen...
issues.justification: The deliberately broken pseudo-German is replaced by (partly) invented, longer German with added content ('Seinen treuen Diener'); the translation adds material not in the source and still doesn't match the Soviet comic mangling.

issues.translation_quote: So what I tell my king?
issues.justification: Deliberately broken ambassador English works, but 'Tell to your king my ardent greetings' is inconsistent; the gag of ambassador's broken speech is only half preserved.

issues.source_quote: Вы представляете, что Вы видели? - Еще бы!
issues.translation_quote: Do you realise what you've just seen? - I sure do!
issues.justification: Register shift: 'I sure do' is American slang for an exchange in which the thief-actor is speaking in a polite, theatrical register, while spelling 'realise' is British; dialect inconsistency.

issues.source_quote: Пусть на обратном пути Казань возьмут.
issues.translation_quote: Let them take Kazan on the way back.
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Ну, чтоб два раза не ездить' is rendered adequately; however 'You were too hasty there' mistranslates 'Это вы поспешили' loosely.

issues.source_quote: Вставай, Федор / Федь, ты брось кланяться
issues.translation_quote: Fedya, quit bowing. At this rate you'll be falling over till nightfall.
issues.justification: Fine, but inconsistent naming of Feofan/Fyodor/Fedya is carried over from source without clarification.

issues.translation_quote: Anise. ... Stolichnaya.
issues.justification: 'Anise' alone is unclear for vodka brand/type (anise-flavoured vodka); minor clarity loss.

issues.translation_quote: Gotta eat something with your drink!
issues.justification: Overly casual American colloquialism ('Gotta') for a period tsar's speech.

issues.source_quote: Оставь меня, старушка, я в печали.
issues.translation_quote: Leave me, old woman, I am in sorrow.
issues.justification: Stiff register; the source is a drunk's mock-poetic line from a well-known song/film quote.

issues.translation_quote: Whither?!
issues.justification: Dialect/mistaken 'куды' is a comic vulgar word of a peasant-like speaker; 'Whither' is too elevated.

issues.translation_quote: Kisses! Drive on!
issues.justification: Fine overall; minor naturalness issue.

issues.translation_quote: I'll be sitting out a long sentence soon enough.
issues.justification: The pun 'сесть' (sit down to a dissertation / go to prison) is replaced by an addition ('a long sentence'), making the joke explicit and altering it.

issues.translation_quote: You see, the other one has a smarter face!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but earlier 'Вот лица попрошу не касаться' rendered fine; minor.

issues.source_quote: Там что такое? А, почки заячьи верченые.
issues.translation_quote: Ah, spit-roasted hare kidneys.
issues.justification: 'верченые' is a period-style term and 'One kidneys for the Tsaritsa' is ungrammatical, creating unintended awkwardness.

issues.translation_quote: Verily, forasmuch... I'm most grateful to you!
issues.justification: The comic contrast of archaic Church Slavonic filler with Soviet bureaucratic politeness is partially preserved, but 'Verily' is a stock fantasy-archaism.
